decisions.reason: The source also requires translating the Hero V gesture into the É accent, but that impact is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The Hero V final-stretch refinement is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; deriving the second V from that gesture does not otherwise change Hero V geometry.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already records the final-stretch focus and joint evaluation of the gesture across the Hero V, second V, and É accent.
Translating the Hero V gesture into the lowercase v and É accent does not change the deferred architectural construction of the E and L letterforms.
The source changes the second V's geometric derivation but does not alter its smaller, subordinate visual prominence relative to the Hero V.
The geometry-derivation decision does not modify the deferred champagne material treatment or its role.
The shared right-arm gesture does not change the deferred requirement for cohesive wordmark kerning.
The source design decision does not alter the independent obligation to include design rationale with review rounds.
The glyph-geometry decision has no effect on acceptable proof attachment formats.
